newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Great Ocean sees fall in '96 net.
newsitem.headline: China's Great Ocean sees fall in '96 net.

text.p: Shenzhen Great Ocean Shipping Co Ltd said net profits declined in 1996 as its core business -- marine container transport -- was affected by China's relatively sluggish exports, a spokesman said on Wednesday.

The company estimated 1996 after-tax profits would be lower than 43 million yuan versus 50.39 million yuan in 1995 and 39.75 million yuan in 1994, the company spokesman told the Hong Kong-based China Securities Bulletin newsletter.
Precise profits figures would not be made public until an audit was completed, he said.
But the firm expected strong growth in net earnings in 1997 due to a recovery in China's exports and company expansions, the official said without elaborating further.
Earlier this month, the firm said in a statement that it planned to issue 50 million new foreign currency B shares in 1997 and to list them on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange.

The offer, tentatively priced at between HK$2.50-3.50 per share, requires approval from shareholders due to meet in Shenzhen on February 12, it said. The plan is subject to final approval from the China Securities Regulatory Commission.
If that was successful, it would use funds raised from the second B share offer to buy container vessels, it said.
